english: Let $P$ be a point on the parabola $x^{2}=4y$ such that exactly two distinct lines passing through $P$ are tangent to the curve $y=x^{3}$. Then the $y$-intercept of the tangent to the parabola $x^{2}=4y$ at $P$ is equal to
hindi: माना कि $P$ परवलय $x^{2}=4y$ पर एक ऐसा बिन्दु है कि $P$ से होकर जाने वाली ठीक दो भिन्न रेखाएँ वक्र $y=x^{3}$ की स्पर्श रेखाएँ हैं। तब परवलय $x^{2}=4y$ के बिन्दु $P$ पर खींची गई स्पर्श रेखा का $y$-अन्तःखण्ड बराबर है
solution: Take $P(2s,s^{2})$ (slope form: the tangent of slope $s$ touches $x^{2}=4y$ at $(2s,s^{2})$; its equation is $y=sx-s^{2}$).
Tangent to $y=x^{3}$ at $(a,a^{3})$ passes through $(h,k)$ iff $g(a)=2a^{3}-3ha^{2}+k=0$; each real root $a$ gives one tangent.
$g'(a)=6a(a-h)$; critical values $g(0)=k$, $g(h)=k-h^{3}$. Exactly two distinct roots $\Leftrightarrow$ a double root $\Leftrightarrow k=0$ or $k=h^{3}$ (but not both).
$k=0\Rightarrow s=0$: then $h=k=0$ and $g=2a^{3}$ has one root only, rejected.
$k=h^{3}$: $s^{2}=8s^{3}\Rightarrow s=\dfrac{1}{8}$, $P\left(\dfrac{1}{4},\dfrac{1}{64}\right)$ (it lies on $y=x^{3}$; roots $a=\frac14,\frac14,-\frac18$, two tangents).
Tangent to the parabola at $P$: $y=\dfrac{x}{8}-\dfrac{1}{64}$, so the $y$-intercept is $-\dfrac{1}{64}$.
solution_full: Any point of $x^{2}=4y$ can be written as $P(2s,s^{2})$. Since $y'=\dfrac{x}{2}$, the tangent at $P$ has slope $s$, and its equation is $y-s^{2}=s(x-2s)$, that is $y=sx-s^{2}$ (slope form of the tangent of $x^{2}=4y$).
Write $P=(h,k)$ with $h=2s$, $k=s^{2}$. The tangent to $y=x^{3}$ at $(a,a^{3})$ is $y-a^{3}=3a^{2}(x-a)$. It passes through $(h,k)$ iff $k-a^{3}=3a^{2}(h-a)$, i.e. $g(a)=2a^{3}-3ha^{2}+k=0$.

Different real roots $a$ give different tangent lines (the slopes $3a^{2}$ with the intercepts $-2a^{3}$ differ), so the number of tangents through $P$ equals the number of distinct real roots of $g$.
$g'(a)=6a^{2}-6ha=6a(a-h)$, so for $h\neq 0$ the critical points are $a=0$ and $a=h$, with $g(0)=k$ and $g(h)=k-h^{3}$.
A cubic has three distinct real roots when $g(0)g(h)<0$, one real root when $g(0)g(h)>0$, and exactly two distinct roots (one of them double) when exactly one of $g(0)$, $g(h)$ is zero.
Case $k=0$: $s^{2}=0\Rightarrow s=0$, so $P=(0,0)$; then $h=0$ and $g(a)=2a^{3}$ has the single root $a=0$. Only one tangent, so this case is rejected.
Case $k=h^{3}$: $s^{2}=8s^{3}\Rightarrow s^{2}(8s-1)=0\Rightarrow s=\dfrac{1}{8}$ (as $s\neq 0$). Then $P=\left(\dfrac{1}{4},\dfrac{1}{64}\right)$, which lies on $y=x^{3}$.
Check: $g(a)=2a^{3}-\dfrac{3}{4}a^{2}+\dfrac{1}{64}=2\left(a-\dfrac14\right)^{2}\left(a+\dfrac18\right)$, so the two tangents are those at $a=\frac14$ and $a=-\frac18$.
For every other $s$, $g(0)=s^{2}>0$ and $g(h)=s^{2}(1-8s)$ is non-zero, so the count is 1 or 3; hence $P$ is unique.
The tangent to the parabola at $P$ is $y=\dfrac{1}{8}x-\dfrac{1}{64}$; its $y$-intercept is $-\dfrac{1}{64}$.
originality_note: New: points of a parabola classified by the number of tangents they send to a cubic (way 5: the point turns out to be where the parabola meets the cubic). Closest known: number of tangents from (h,k) to y = x^3. Different because: the external point is constrained to a parabola and the double-root case (k = h^3 or k = 0) must be recognised and the origin rejected.

justification: Two ideas linked: root counting of the tangent cubic via critical values, and the parametric/slope form of the parabola; the rejected origin case is the trap. Comparable to the sign analysis of 2026-P1-Q1 (L3); as an SCQ with options it stays at 3.
